title: Responsive token behavior audit: iOS Safari & Android Firefox — triage and remediation plan
creator: Ethan Kim
body:
Purpose: Run a focused, platform-sensitive QA pass against our UI kit tokens and key components (buttons, tables, charts) to identify cross-browser / responsive regressions that only surface on iOS Safari and Firefox on Android. This ticket consolidates findings from the exploratory pass, triages by severity, and defines concrete remediation steps and owners.

Scope:
- Design tokens: spacing, typography, color tokens (CSS custom properties mapping), density tokens and fractional px handling.
- Buttons: sizing, touch targets, focus ring rendering, disabled state contrast.
- Tables: sticky headers, column overflow/wrapping, zebra stripes, header alignment with sort icons.
- Charts: canvas scaling, device pixel ratio (DPR) rounding, legend wrapping, tooltip positioning on touch.
- Responsive behaviors: breakpoint token application, container queries behavior, and mobile orientation flips (portrait <-> landscape).

Notes on approach:
- This is a design-led QA with engineering pairing for repro/PR creation. Use device farm + local devices where possible. For each issue we must include: clear repro steps, screenshots, root cause hypothesis (design token vs runtime CSS vs JS), suggested fix, and a proposed owner (Design or ENG).
acceptance_criteria: All reproduceable issues from exploratory pass are captured with steps, severity, and owner assignment
High and P1 regressions have proposed fixes and linked engineering tickets or PRs
Design token mapping doc updated with platform caveats for Safari and Firefox
QA checklist and automated visual regression tests (Percy/Gal) items created for remaining low/medium issues
steps_to_reproduce: Open Redwood UI kit demo page (https://redwood-internal.dev/ui-kit) in iOS Safari 16.4 on iPhone 13. Note button baseline alignment and font rendering in Compact density.
Open same page in Firefox 110 on Pixel 6 Android. Rotate to landscape and check table header stickiness while scrolling long lists.
In Chrome on mac, set DPR to 2 and compare chart canvas render vs iOS Safari to spot DPR rounding mismatches.
Toggle reduced-motion & high-contrast to validate focus outline rendering and disabled states across browsers.
findings: Typography tokens (token--body-md, token--line-height) render with different line-height rounding on iOS Safari causing 1–2px vertical layout shifts in stacked components.
CSS variable fallback order causes color token mismatches in Firefox when using :root overrides for themes (dark mode).
Button touch targets on small devices occasionally measure <44px after fractional padding adjustments; observed on iOS only when font-scaling is enabled.
Sticky table header jumps when a table cell has subpixel fractional height; occurs in Firefox Android when header is position: sticky and parent uses transform for container queries.

Canvas charts show aliasing and blurry lines on iOS unless explicit DPR scaling is applied in draw routine; mouse hover tooltip positioning on touch devices also misaligned due to pointer vs touch coordinate mismatch.
Focus ring (outline) is clipped inside rounded buttons in Safari due to overflow: hidden on the container — reduces visible keyboard focus area for accessibility users.
Z-index stacking context differences between browsers cause popover legends on charts to appear under header bars in Firefox (Android) in specific breakpoints.
remediation_plan:
Priority A (P0/P1) fixes:
- ENG-4092: Normalize line-height rendering by switching token mapping to unitless line-height and adding platform-specific CSS where necessary. Owner: ENG (frontend).
- ENG-4021: Button padding and touch-target enforcement: clamp computed touch area to minimum 44x44 via pseudo-element hit area. Owner: ENG + Design review.
- Create chart-utils PR to explicitly set canvas.width/height based on window.devicePixelRatio and redraw on orientation change. Owner: ENG-graphics.

Priority B (P2) fixes:
- Update theme token fallback order to explicit color-scheme CSS and test in Firefox. Owner: Design + ENG.
- For sticky table issue, remove transform on parent or change sticky context to use top with will-change: transform fallback; add regression test. Owner: ENG.

Priority C (P3) and polish:
- Adjust focus ring rendering by moving outlines to an inner focus-visible element and avoid clipping from overflow: hidden. Owner: Design + ENG.
- Add visual regression snapshots for iOS Safari and Firefox Android build targets. Owner: DX/QA.
comments: 2026-03-10 — Ethan Kim: Initial exploratory pass completed on iPhone 13 (iOS 16.4) and Pixel 6 (Android 13). Collected 18 candidate issues; 7 are platform-specific. Attaching screenshots.

2026-03-11 — Diego Morales (ENG): Paired on repro for sticky header. Hypothesis: transform on parent (container query polyfill) is creating new stacking context — will prototype removing transform for a perf check.
2026-03-11 — Maya Patel: Prioritizing touch-target and accessibility issues as P1. Will update token doc to call out unitless line-heights for mobile in the design tokens spec.
2026-03-12 — QA (Priya Singh): Added Percy snapshots for the affected button states and table scroll; some diffs flagged as expected due to platform aliasing — annotated in Drive.
2026-03-13 — Product (Ava Chen): Confirmed high priority for accessibility regressions; suggested we bundle fixes into ui-kit-2026.03 minor release to avoid cascading regressions for customers.
